product_brief: Apple's platform security framework for code signing, app security, and quantum-secure cryptography across iOS, macOS, and other OS.
pqc_capability_description: Apple uses hybrid cryptography combining classic and post-quantum algorithms. Deployed iMessage PQ3 in iOS 17.4, iPadOS 17.4, macOS 14.4, watchOS 10.4. Supports quantum-secure TLS, HTTPS, VPN, SSH, and Apple Watch encryption in iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS 26, tvOS 26, watchOS 26. CryptoKit supports ML-KEM 768/1024 and ML-DSA-65/87.
crypto_primitives: RSA, Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman, Elliptic Curve signature, ML-KEM, ML-DSA
pqc_roadmap_details: Deployed iMessage PQ3 in iOS 17.4, iPadOS 17.4, macOS 14.4, watchOS 10.4. Supports quantum-secure TLS, HTTPS, VPN, SSH, and Apple Watch encryption in iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS 26, tvOS 26, watchOS 26. CryptoKit supports ML-KEM 768/1024 and ML-DSA-65/87.
implementation_attack_surface: Classic algorithms hardened against side-channel attacks exploiting CPU signals.

platform_name: Certicom Code Signing and Key Management Server
product_brief: A secure key management platform that protects signing keys, signs/encrypts software images, and logs key usage for code signing.
pqc_capability_description: The system supports quantum resistant digital signature algorithms and is suitable for quantum-resistant signatures and hybrid schemes. It addresses the threat of cryptographic key cracking by quantum computers with support for new quantum resistant signature algorithms.
crypto_primitives: RSA, ECDSA, quantum resistant digital signature algorithms, NIST approved key derivation, encryption, and key wrapping algorithms
key_management_model: HSM-backed (FIPS 140-2 certified hardware security modules), offline isolated security bunker, web-service based APIs
target_industries: Device manufacturers, IoT (implied by "protecting devices", "secure boot", "OTA services")
signature_schemes: RSA, ECDSA, quantum resistant digital signature algorithms

product_brief: A tool for code signing and software integrity verification, supporting PE, APPX, MSI, and JavaScript files.
pqc_capability_description: The document contains no mention of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), quantum-resistant algorithms, or migration plans. It focuses on classical cryptographic operations using OpenSSL.
crypto_primitives: SHA-256 (default hash function), PKCS#11, PKCS#7, CNG (Cryptography API: Next Generation)
key_management_model: PKCS#11 provider support, CNG engine support, hardware engine support via "-engineCtrl"
primary_platforms: Unix, macOS, Windows (MinGW), Linux (Ubuntu mentioned in testing)
signature_schemes: Not stated (mentions signing and verification, but specific signature algorithms like ECDSA/RSA are not explicitly listed, only hash functions and key management interfaces)
implementation_attack_surface: Integer overflows in APPX processing, double-free vulnerabilities in APPX processing, memory corruption in PE page hash computation, buffer overflow in message digest extraction, memory corruption fixes.
testing_&_validation_methods: GitHub Actions CI, testing framework improvements, tests for python-cryptography compatibility.
qrng_&_entropy_sources: Not stated (mentions pseudo-random NONCE in TSA request)
supply_chain_&_vendor_risk: Removed libcurl dependency (v2.9), uses OpenSSL 3.0+ providers, CMake build system.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Breaking changes in options (e.g., "-st" renamed to "-time", "-timestamp-expiration" removed), compatibility with OpenSSL 3.0+ required for PKCS#11.

pqc_capability_description: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 (RHEL 10) includes support for ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA in core libraries like OpenSSL and NSS. RHEL 10.1 is the first major distribution to start signing RPM packages with post-quantum keys (ML-DSA).
pqc_roadmap_details: PQC support shipped in RHEL 10 in May 2025. RHEL 10.1 signs RPM packages with ML-DSA. Planning began after NIST PQC competition winners announcement in July 2022.
